text:
rachel: Noticed a regression in US canary after last week's bundle split. Charts (sparklines + heatmap) are stuttering on first open. Frame drops and TTFP is up ~200ms. Anyone else seeing this?

tom: I saw a couple of alerts this morning for increased main-thread busy time from the telemetry client. Need a quick repro HAR to correlate.

anika: I ran a quick local canary with the split bundle (dynamic-imports enabled) and observed an extra 90KB in main.chunk and more parse time. But the bigger hit seems to be repeated fetches for /tile between client-worker and main thread.

paul: That's odd; we recently changed the routing policy that pins tile requests to worker-level routing for affinity. Could be a misrouted header causing the worker to skip the cache.

rachel: Repro steps I used: open a dashboard with 12 small tiles, clear site data, load -> cold loads spike, then subsequent navigation still shows occasional parse spikes. Attaching small flamegraph (link): https://redwood-internal/share/flame-sparkline-mar2026.zip

tom: Quick question: are we double-counting telemetry events and using that to decide prefetch eligibility? I remember a change to dedupe telemetry before using it for predictions.

anika: We dedupe server-side but client predictor still emits local hints. If the worker doesn't receive the hint due to header drop, it won't prefetch. I traced the request path: main thread emits hint -> postMessage to worker -> worker triggers fetch with affinity header `X-Affinity: on`. In failing canary cases the header is missing.

paul: That points to a worker-msg serialization issue introduced in the chunk split where the message envelope grew and hit structured-clone edge-case. The header builder uses a Map that may not clone correctly in some browsers.

rachel: Which browsers seeing this? Our synthetic runs were Chrome 114 and Firefox 102.

paul: Mainly Chrome variants so far. I have a small patch that switches the header builder to a plain object and stringifies deterministically before postMessage. Patch: `prefetch.worker.postMessage({type:'hint', headers: JSON.stringify(headersPlain)})`.

tom: Before we patch, could we do a scoped rollback of the bundle-split on canary (small revert) to confirm? If revert fixes it, we can PR the worker fix.

deploy-bot: revert-deploy 2026-03-20T09:12:05 - console-canary/bundle-split-experiment -> us-canary (initiated by tom)

canary-bot: canary deploy complete. Running 10-min synthetic trace.

rachel: Early numbers after revert show TTFP back down ~180ms on the synthetic trace. So bundle split change highly suspicious.

anika: I'll open PR for the worker header serialisation patch and add unit tests for structured-clone safe payloads. Also adding a metric `prefetch_worker_header_missing` so we can detect this in future rollouts.

paul: Also propose a conservative server-side fallback: if worker prefetch hint missing, server returns a short `Link: <.../prefetch>; rel=prefetch` header for the initial tile response for 30s so clients can benefit while we stabilize.

tom: Can we gate that fallback to canary and opt-in via feature-flag? We'll avoid global perf changes.

anika: Yes. I'll add `server.prefetch_fallback=true` for canary only. Tests: local + ci synthetic harness (tile-heavy).

rachel: Follow-ups: PR #4120 (worker header stringify + tests), feature flag for server fallback on canary, metric `prefetch_worker_header_missing`, revert confirmed. I'll file an incident note and update the rollout playbook.

paul: Thanks. TL;DR: bundle split caused structured-clone edge-case -> worker lost affinity headers -> prefetches missed -> cold tile loads and parse spikes. Revert on canary validated. Patch + metric + canary fallback planned.
